deepveinasbestos:handbook-fireproofing-t:
Fireproofing
For when "just don't light it" isn't enough

Wood is a wonderful material. Abundant, easy to work with, and great for adding warmth and color to your builds. Unfortunately, it has one major weakness: fire. That's where asbestos comes in.

Asbestos is a naturally fibrous mineral found in two main forms: Chrysotile and Amosite. Both types occur within sedimentary rock and can be ground into asbestos fibers using a mill.

After grounding asbestos ore into fibers, the resulting asbestos fibers can be soaked in a barrel to create asbestos pulp, which can then be crafted into asbestos paper - a specialized material used to completely fireproof wooden blocks. You can apply it by looking at a block and pressing leftmouse to line it with asbestos and protect it from burning.

Additionally, due to its fibrous texture, asbestos fibers can also serve as an alternative source for flax fibers, making it useful in a variety of use cases.
deepveinasbestos:handbook-asbestos-text:
Asbestos
Its great or fireproofing! but uhh, try not to breath it in..

Asbestos is a naturally occurring fibrous silicate mineral found in six distinct varieties, each forming under unique conditions. These are Chrysotile, Amosite, Tremolite, Anthophyllite, Actinolite, and the rarest, Crocidolite.

Chrysotile
The most common form of asbestos, Chrysotile is the main source of white asbestos and is typically found near the surface in peridotite or some forms of sedimentary rock. Its fibers are long and flexible, making it perfect for producing twine.

Amosite
Amosite is a type of brown asbestos that forms beneath rich hematite and magnetite deposits. It is tougher and coarser than Chrysotile and provides a more durable, heat-resistant fiber.Amosite is ideal for asbestos bricks and making fireclay.

Tremolite
Tremolite is a rarer and more valuable asbestos that can be found in peridotite. It can appear in two forms: tremolite crystals and tremolite asbestiform. The fibrous form can be ground into white asbestos, while the crystalline variety is a valuable gem that can be sold to traders.

Anthophyllite
Anthophyllite is a contaminant mineral commonly found intermixed with soapstone. Because it is a brown asbestos that can occur in surface-level soapstone deposits, it serves as a useful early-game substitute for Amosite.

Crocidolite
Crocidolite, also known as blue asbestos, is the rarest and most heat-resistant form of asbestos. It forms deep underground in igneous rock. Its fibers are extremely fine, strong, and chemically stable, making it necessary for the highest tier of refractory bricks and fire-resistant textiles.


Fireproofing
The primary use of asbestos is fireproofing. All forms of asbestos fibers can be soaked to create asbestos pulp, which is then processed into asbestos paper. Asbestos paper can be applied to wooden blocks with leftmouse to completely protect them from igniting.
